_what: What a Marketplace tool run on this computer may reach (harness/wake-handlers/tool-reach.mjs). A tool's descriptor declares `reach`, a list of { kind, ... } rows; each kind is a row in `kinds` below, whose `allow` lines are sandbox rules added to the base profile with {path} and {port} filled from the declared row. `base` is what every run gets ({ancestors} are the folders above its own folder and its program, which a program may look at but not list): the system as macOS ships it, its own folder, and nothing of the person's (their home folder, other disks) and no network. `protected_roots` are the person's places a run cannot read or write unless it declares them; `~` is this computer's home folder. `asks: true` means the person's approval is needed before a tool from another maker runs with that reach (tool-reach-approvals.json in the helper's folder, one row per tool, files fingerprint and reach); a tool this account saved, or one Trillion ships (made_by shared), runs with what it declared. `enforced` says whether macOS itself refuses what was not declared (`kernel`) or the declaration is only shown and approved (`declared`): microphone, camera, files and network are refused by the kernel; Accessibility and screen reading follow the app's own macOS grants. `env` names values the run is started with. A kind with `proxy` gets a local socket in the run's own folder ({socket}) that forwards each HTTP request to this computer's Trillion with this computer's key attached, so a tool that declared `trillion` acts in the person's Trillion without ever holding the key and without any internet reach. Adding a kind is a row here. `network-hosts` lets a run reach only the hosts it names (a comma list, `*.name` for a whole domain) through a loopback proxy that records every decision (harness/wake-handlers/egress-proxy.mjs); the profile lets the run connect to that proxy and nothing else. `exec` is what a run may start: `mode` "open" (the default) puts no limit on programs, "allowlist" adds a kernel rule that starts nothing but the run's own folder, its interpreter, /usr/bin/env, the program the descriptor names and the `allow` rows ({ path, match: literal | subpath }); the same rows say, in words, which programs the run has (describeRun), so the description and the fence cannot drift. `argument_rules` are checked against the command before it starts: `deny_regex` refuses a command of `command` (its program's file name, or * for any) whose arguments match; `only_values` refuses one whose value after `flag` is not in `values` (an empty list refuses any value). A row is off until `enabled` is true; a refusal is said in its `message`.

accessibility.said: read and control other apps through Accessibility

screen.said: see what is on the screen

trillion.said: act in your Trillion as this computer

environment.said: see the {name} setting of this computer

environment.what: The variables a tool run sees. The run starts with an empty environment plus the names in `allow` (taken from this computer's own environment when it has them) and the names the tool declared with an `environment` reach, so a key in the helper's environment never reaches a tool that did not ask for it. `mode` "inherit" gives the run the helper's whole environment as before.

argument_rules.message: find with -exec, -execdir, -ok or -okdir is not allowed: it starts any program.
This run may not start an agent of that type.
